The compass pays Solanthis for having thought about it beforehand. Almost nothing on it improves his own turn; nearly all of it spends his reaction on somebody else's.

Wondrous item and arcane focus, legacy item (requires attunement by Solanthis)

Your Charges

The Promise Charges pool grows on its own at 6th, 10th and 15th level. You never have to update the sheet — the number just changes.

StateYour levelPromise ChargesBack at dawn
Dormantlevels 3–53all of them
Awakenedlevels 6–95all of them
Exaltedlevels 10–1471d6 + 1
Legendarylevel 15+91d8 + 1

At Dormant and Awakened every spent charge comes back. From 10th level it stops refilling completely: the pool is bigger, and a heavy day stays expensive into the next one.

Legacy Save DC

Where a feature makes something roll a saving throw, the DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier. It comes off your sheet, so it rises as you do.

What Unlocks When

Features arrive on their own. Below its level a feature is not on the item at all, so anything you can see on the sheet is something you can use. Where a later state improves an earlier feature, the old version disappears and the new one takes its place.

Dormant — levels 3–5 (Uncommon): The Compass; Forewarned; Not Them; Prepared Mind.

Awakened — levels 6–9 (Rare): I Planned for This; Contingency Pocket; Calculated Intervention.

Exalted — levels 10–14 (Very Rare): Contingency; No One Gets Left Behind; There Was Another Way.

Legendary — level 15+ (Legendary): Grand Contingency; I Accounted for That; The Promise.

Advancing

Reaching the level makes the next state possible. What actually wakes the item is the moment named at the top of each state below — a choice, not an achievement, and never something you can win in a fight. You do not need to chase it. When it happens, you will know, and so will the item.

Uncommon · levels 3–5 · 3 Promise Charges, all of them returning at dawn

Where it starts. This is the item as you first receive it. Everything below is yours from the moment you attune.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

The Compass

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

The brass compass serves as an arcane focus. Its needle points toward whichever creature within 60 feet Solanthis sincerely believes is in the greatest immediate physical danger. This gives no supernatural knowledge of hidden creatures.

Forewarned

Passive. Always on, handled by an effect on the item. Nothing to click.

Solanthis gains a +1 bonus to initiative and cannot be surprised while conscious.

Not Them

Reaction — 1 charge

When a creature Solanthis can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack, he can use his reaction and expend 1 charge to grant it +2 AC against the triggering attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss.

Prepared Mind

Reaction — 1× per long rest

At the end of each long rest, choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder. Once before Solanthis' next long rest, when he or a creature within 30 feet takes the selected damage type, he can use his reaction to grant that creature resistance to the triggering damage.

Rare · levels 6–9 · 5 Promise Charges, all of them returning at dawn

What wakes it. Solanthis possesses the means to force someone to follow what he believes is the correct course, and deliberately allows that person to make the decision themselves.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

I Planned for This

Reaction — 2 charges

When a creature Solanthis can see within 30 feet fails a saving throw, he can use his reaction and expend 2 charges to allow it to reroll. The new roll must be used.

Contingency Pocket

Action — 1× per long rest

Once per long rest, Solanthis may produce a mundane object he could reasonably have acquired. It must cost no more than 25 gp, weigh no more than 10 pounds, fit inside a backpack, and not be a weapon, armour, poison or spell component with a listed cost. It disappears at the next dawn if not consumed or destroyed. Narratively, he prepared it earlier.

Calculated Intervention

Not Them (Calculated Intervention). Reaction — 1 charge

Not Them improves: when it turns the attack into a miss, the protected creature may immediately move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. This replaces the Dormant version of Not Them.

Very Rare · levels 10–14 · 7 Promise Charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Solanthis accepts a serious personal risk because his preparation can protect others, despite having a safer option available to him.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Contingency

No action — 1× per long rest

After a long rest, Solanthis may designate two willing creatures, including himself, that he can see. For each, choose one contingency:

  • Escape. When reduced below half hit points, the creature may immediately move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  • Brace. When it fails a Strength, Dexterity or Constitution saving throw, it adds 1d6, potentially succeeding.
  • Mind. When it fails an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma saving throw, it adds 1d6, potentially succeeding.
  • Endure. When reduced to 0 hit points without being killed outright, it drops to 1 hit point instead.

Each contingency triggers once and then disappears. A creature can have only one at a time.

No One Gets Left Behind

Action — 3 charges — 1 minute, concentration

As an action, Solanthis can expend 3 charges. For 1 minute a 20-foot-radius protective field moves with him, and while inside it his allies ignore nonmagical difficult terrain, have advantage on death saving throws, cannot have their speed reduced below 10 feet unless incapacitated, and gain +1 AC. He must concentrate on this as though concentrating on a spell.

There Was Another Way

No action — 1× per short or long rest

When Solanthis casts a spell that deals damage, he may choose any number of creatures he can see to automatically succeed on their saving throws against that spell and take no damage if they would normally take half. Once used, this cannot be used again until a short or long rest.

Legendary · level 15+ · 9 Promise Charges, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Solanthis faces a situation in which imposing his will would genuinely be easier and possibly safer, but finds a way to protect people without taking their agency from them.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Grand Contingency

No action — 1× per long rest

Solanthis can maintain contingencies on a number of creatures equal to his proficiency bonus rather than two. This replaces Contingency.

I Accounted for That

Reaction — 1× per long rest

Once per long rest, after a creature Solanthis can see within 60 feet rolls a natural 1, suffers a critical hit, fails a saving throw or is reduced to 0 hit points, he can use his reaction and declare that he prepared for precisely this possibility. Choose one:

  • the natural 1 becomes a 10;
  • the critical hit becomes a normal hit;
  • the failed save is rerolled with advantage;
  • the creature drops to 1 hit point.

The Promise

Action — 1× per long rest — 1 minute, concentration

Once per long rest, as an action, Solanthis chooses up to six willing creatures within 30 feet. For 1 minute each gains resistance to one damage type chosen individually when this begins, +2 AC, advantage on death saving throws, and immunity to being frightened. Solanthis gains none of these benefits. The effect requires concentration. At his absolute strongest, his greatest magic is still about everyone else getting home.

The compass pays Solanthis for having thought about it beforehand. Almost nothing on it improves his own turn; nearly all of it spends his reaction on somebody else's.

At the Table

  • Ask for the attack total before spending Not Them. It is +2 AC against an attack that has already been rolled, and a hit that misses by one is the entire point of the feature.
  • Prepared Mind is free. It costs no charge and resets every long rest, so choosing a damage type is pure profit. Never skip it — pick whatever the party expects to walk into.
  • He cannot run two auras. No One Gets Left Behind and The Promise both need concentration, and so does any concentration spell. Decide before initiative which job he has this fight.
  • The Promise deliberately excludes him. That is not an oversight, and it is most of why it is worth an action.
  • Contingency is declared in advance, after a long rest. Endure on whoever stands in front is almost always right; Brace or Mind on whoever has the worst save.

Questions That Come Up

Does Not Them stack with the Shield spell?
Yes. They are separate bonuses to the same AC against the same attack, and both apply.

Can I Planned for This be used on an enemy's failed save?
It says any creature he can see, so yes — if he can think of a reason he would want to.

Can Contingency Pocket produce a healing potion?
No. It is mundane gear worth 25 gp or less; a potion is a magic item.

Can one creature hold two contingencies?
No. One at a time, and it vanishes once it triggers.

Does Forewarned mean he cannot be ambushed at all?
He cannot be surprised while conscious, which means he acts normally in the first round. The ambush still happens.

If Something Here Disagrees With the Item

The item on your sheet is the rules. This journal is generated from the same source, so the two should never differ — but if they do, the item wins and your DM should know.
